items.summary: Everything that pg_memtable stores lives in shared memory, and a restart of the server destroys it, but the handle is left in the catalog. Since nothing special is done to inform Postgres that tables that use the memtable table access method (MemTables) do not survive a restart, it will treat the table as permanent, with “interesting” consequences. In this post you’ll learn about table persistence, how unlogged tables deal with a server restart, how to make every MemTable unlogged so that Postgres handles MemTables correctly, and how to recreate the arena of a table after a restart. In Part 8 you could see how a backend lets go of an arena t…
